feed.title: Control and Automation for Intelligent Systems Lab
feed.subtitle: Research in the Control and Automation for Intelligent Systems Lab focuses on developing, analyzing, and applying control theory and artificial intelligence to improve the safety, flexibility, and performance of complex, dynamic systems, such as manufacturing systems.

entry.title: Welcome Vaibhav Shrivastav
entry.content:
Welcome to Vaibhav Shrivastav, who has joined the lab as a Doctor of Engineering (D.Eng.) candidate in Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering, advised by Prof. Ilya Kovalenko!

His research focuses on AI-driven agents for decision-making, coordination, and verification across engineering, product development, and manufacturing processes, with an emphasis on reliable, transparent, and trustworthy AI-assisted decisions.
entry.summary: Welcome to Vaibhav Shrivastav, who has joined the lab as a Doctor of Engineering (D.Eng.) candidate in Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering, advised by Prof. Ilya Kovalenko!

entry.title: Seminar at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

link.title: Seminar at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

entry.content:
On October 13, 2026, Dr. Ilya Kovalenko delivered the seminar “Control and Automation Architectures for Adaptive and Safe Manufacturing Systems” at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, hosted by the Department of Mechanical Science and Engineering.

His talk explored how model-based, adaptive, and distributed control strategies can improve manufacturing flexibility while supporting safe and predictable operation, with examples from simulations and experimental testbeds.

Read more on the Illinois MechSE seminar event page.
entry.summary: On October 13, 2026, Dr. Ilya Kovalenko delivered the seminar “Control and Automation Architectures for Adaptive and Safe Manufacturing Systems” at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, hosted by the Department of Mechanical Science and Engineering.

entry.title: Seminar for Argonne National Laboratory
entry.content:
On October 1, 2026, Dr. Ilya Kovalenko delivered the virtual seminar “Developing Control and Automation Approaches for Adaptive and Flexible Manufacturing Systems” as part of Argonne National Laboratory’s LANS Seminar series.

His talk covered the lab’s work on AI-assisted human–robot collaboration, coordinating manufacturing subsystems, and adapting production to changes in power availability and customer demand.

Read more on the Argonne National Laboratory event page.

entry.title: IEEE International Conference on Automation Science and Engineering (CASE 2026)

link.title: IEEE International Conference on Automation Science and Engineering (CASE 2026)

entry.content:
Jiabao presented their research at the IEEE International Conference on Automation Science and Engineering (CASE 2026) in Shenyang, China.

Our work explores how Large Language Models (LLMs) can enable more intuitive human–robot collaboration in manufacturing. In particular, we developed a framework that allows a human operator to use verbal guidance to teach a robot new assembly tasks, connecting natural-language instructions with executable robotic skills and trajectories.
entry.summary: Jiabao presented their research at the IEEE International Conference on Automation Science and Engineering (CASE 2026) in Shenyang, China.
